cap: After about 16 weeks amniotic fluid is mostly fetal urine, and the fetus clears it by swallowing, so the volume reflects the fetal kidneys and gut. Too little urine, as in bilateral renal agenesis, gives oligohydramnios, a flat face with limb deformities and fatal pulmonary hypoplasia (the Potter sequence). Failed swallowing, fetal diuresis from maternal diabetes, anemia or twins give polyhydramnios.
